messages:
Anya: FYI — Aegis Health just confirmed an enterprise commit. Need a POC capacity plan + preheat/runway. POC starts next Mon. They expect bursty peaks: ~350 rps for 20-40s, steady 35-45 rps otherwise. Asking for reserved vs burst sizing and autoscale fallbacks.
Devon: Can you paste their traffic profile (payload sizes + token distributions) and SLA targets?
Anya: Dropping the quick profile: avg prompt ~45 tokens, avg generation ~120 tokens, occasional long job ~800 tokens. 95th latency target < 400ms. Will upload CSV to the deal folder.
Martin: Quick gut calc: steady 40 rps -> ~2 GPUs if using a 70B quantized variant with good KV cache hit. Spikes to 350 rps need either a prewarmed burst pool (~6 GPUs) or autoscale with warmup + queuing. Recommend reserved 6 GPUs + autoscale down to 2, or reserved 3 + larger burst credits depending on their cost appetite.
Lina: Which model variant are they planning? For 8-bit quant on A100-type hardware we estimate ~50-70 rps/GPU at ~1k tokens depending on kernels. KV cache warm hits can net ~1.5-1.8x throughput. If they can accept slightly smaller model for fallbacks we can reduce reserved footprint.
Anya: They said open-70B-quant. Also this must be Private (VPC). Can Private support reserved + burst credits like Dedicated?
Martin: Yes — Private supports reserved pools + controlled burst credits. Operational notes: preheat window and a KV warmup job must be scheduled in the customer's VPC; ops will need KMS access for the model artifacts. Note: KMS onboarding adds ~48 hours to timeline.
Devon: Proposed autoscale policy (draft):
```yaml
policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 8
  metric: qps
  target_qps_per_replica: 60
  cool_down_seconds: 60
  prewarm: true
  prewarm_schedule: "cron(0 15 * * ? *)" # 15m before business window
```
Lina: Add an explicit KV warmup step: run ~1k representative requests (from their sample prompts) during preheat. That drastically lowers cold-step latency and increases effective throughput. Also recommend a cheaper fallback model (eg open-13B-quant) with routing policy for graceful degradation.
Martin: Cost tradeoffs: reserved 6 GPUs committed monthly gives best latency guarantee for spikes up to ~280 rps without additional queueing. For 350 rps sustained spikes we'd still rely on burst credits or temporary overprovisioning. I'll run a detailed cost vs SLA matrix.
Anya: Action items: Martin -> cost/runway numbers + fallback model list by EOD. Devon -> preheat job script + staging test by EOD. Lina -> KV warmup recipe + fallback routing config. I'll coordinate customer preheat windows and sign-off. :thumbsup:
Martin: On it. One more ops callout: we'll need to map AZ affinity for their VPC to avoid cross-AZ latency; recommend co-locating reserved pool in their preferred AZs.
SRE-Bot: preheat-job created in staging by Devon at 2026-03-18T08:50Z — test run scheduled for 2026-03-18T09:10Z.
Customersuccess: I'll prepare a short cutover runbook (step-by-step) and notify onboarding.
Anya: Sweet — sync tomorrow 10:30am PT. @Martin please include evict/fallback policy and a short TL;DR for the customer (one-pager they can share with infra).
Devon: Will add an A/B fallback plan: normal -> reserved 70B -> fallback routed to 13B with lower cost per token.
Lina: I'll include perf numbers and sample prompt set for the one-pager.
Anya: Thanks team — will follow up in the deal channel after EOD deliverables.
